resources.string: Save your recovery mnemonic
Export relay archive
Save this chain’s relay archive without recovery envelopes. Signed objects still need verification before restore; this is not a complete recovery archive.
Export with recovery envelopes

Save a relay archive that includes encrypted recovery envelopes. The administrator mnemonic is required for this one export. Protect the file as sensitive ciphertext; its footer is an integrity checksum, not proof that every object is valid.
Export verified checkpoint
Create a signed checkpoint at this device’s highest verified contiguous log position. It proves this device’s view, not that the relay has no later data.
Signed checkpoint saved and read back. Share it only through a user-selected trusted channel.
Checkpoint export cancelled.
The checkpoint could not be signed or read back. No checkpoint was accepted.
Import peer checkpoint
Verify a checkpoint from an already certified device and compare its data prefix and transparency position with retained evidence.
Peer signature, certified device, data prefix, and transparency position verified.
Peer signature and data prefix verified. Its transparency position differs from this device’s verified anchor and remains an unmatched signed view.
A signed peer checkpoint contradicts retained verified history. Writes are paused and both views were retained for investigation.
The checkpoint could not be fully authenticated or compared with retained chain evidence.
Repair from retained verified history
Use the chain administrator mnemonic to submit retained current-generation records with their original verified log entries.

This sends retained current-generation encrypted records and their original signed log entries to the selected relay for repair. Each response receipt and the updated transparency checkpoint are verified before local evidence is stored. Local data is retained if repair is incomplete.

Choose the target relay. This stages control history only; it does not create a writable chain or move records.

Review the target relay and enter the chain administrator mnemonic. The relay policy must be current and consented for that origin. This operation only stages signed control history and returns a staging log ID. It does not commit a new generation or move encrypted records.

Commit relay reseed

This commits a fresh generation on %1$s, retires the old device identity, replays unresolved local outbox operations, and switches this device to that relay. Verify the target before continuing. Enter the administrator mnemonic again to authorize the commit.

Before cutover, pause every other client that can write to the source relay. The relay has no freeze operation. After you confirm, this client verifies a final source suffix immediately before switching. Any write that arrives after that verified suffix stays only on the source and requires explicit reconciliation; it is never copied automatically. Destination: %1$s

Verify recovery archive
Select a complete unpruned generation-0 recovery archive for this chain. Verification is read-only; restoration is offered separately after the archive passes every check.
Recovery archive signatures, transparency evidence, encrypted records, and snapshot parts verified for this pinned chain. No data was installed.
Restore verified archive
Restore

Replay this complete archive into this chain’s local state. The protected authority and transparency head must still match exactly, and there must be no pending uploads or unresolved conflicts. This does not restore onto another device or replace chain authority.
Verify deletion status

Prune verified relay history
Irreversibly remove raw relay entries covered by the latest verified snapshot. Requires a complete current snapshot and root authorization.

This permanently removes the raw relay log prefix through the verified snapshot. The operation is allowed only when the full current state and acceptance evidence are verified; keep independent exports if you need the original event bodies.

The relay and signatures authenticate this snapshot, but cannot prove that its author included every earlier item. Trusting semantic completeness is your decision. The client will verify the snapshot commitment and replay the signed suffix before completing initial sync.

Use the approved QR/file enrollment flow or fetch and verify the already-approved device envelope. Never auto-register a replacement identity.
Free a slot through explicit device revocation and its accepted emergency epoch transaction before retrying enrollment.
Stop writes and compare the pinned origin, log and signed checkpoint. Use verified repair/recovery or an explicitly approved relay migration; never reset the pin from this hint.
Fetch and verify the signed epoch history. Rebuild only unaccepted records; after key expiry, use a complete verified current-key snapshot.
Create a fresh enrollment offer and request; expired or consumed offer IDs cannot be reused.
An eligible sender must resend an authorized device envelope, or a mnemonic holder must recover it. Recovery envelopes are not added through the device-envelope route.
Fetch all referenced parts and verify the complete signed snapshot, or select another verified snapshot/replay path. Preserve evidence; do not prune around missing state.
Fetch the authenticated winner and build a fresh proposal/binding or exact membership bundle. Do not replay a stale signed proposal.
Restart the read from its durable verified progress mark and validate the replacement page before releasing this cursor blocker.
Split the batch into requests that fit the advertised limit. Keep an individually oversized immutable record unchanged and blocked.
Honor Retry-After and jitter. The client retains queued data and does not treat the error text as authority.
Retain the exact request and outbox, then probe signed history/idempotency before any retry after the backoff.

Treat relay-notice and migration_origin only as unsigned suggestions. Select the destination explicitly, then validate its origin, TLS, relay-key pin and complete chain continuity before transfer or cutover.
Address the relay quota or storage condition, then explicitly confirm recovery. The unsigned byte counts are diagnostic hints only.
The accepted object may be awaiting its signed receipt. Retain it and retry the exact receipt lookup after backoff; do not recreate the object.
The exact request is invalid and remains paused. Correct its endpoint, method, media type, filter, cursor or body from the protocol; do not replay unchanged bytes.
Rebuild authorization for the exact method, path, query and body with a fresh valid token. The error does not authorize changing the operation or its binding.

Stop this request and verify the pinned device identity, certified key, signed object, epoch chain and recipient authorization. Use only the approved repair or enrollment flow; never trust the error body as authority.
Compare the authenticated existing chain, record, device, request or import state with local pins. Keep this exact request blocked; never overwrite state or reuse the conflicting immutable ID.
A 410 response alone does not authorize erasure. Fetch GET /deletion and verify its signatures and ledger linkage against the pinned authority before any deletion action.
